claims.claim_text: In May 2025 Opendoor issued $325 million aggregate principal of 7.00% convertible senior notes due 2030 ($246M via debt exchange of 2026 Notes plus $79M for cash) in privately negotiated transactions.
claims.source_quote: In May 2025, the Company entered into privately negotiated transactions with certain holders of the 0.25% convertible senior notes due in 2026 (the 2026 Notes) and new investors, pursuant to which the Company issued $325 million aggregate principal amount of 7.00% convertible senior notes due 2030
claims.subject: Opendoor Technologies Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: A May 2025 8-K announcing the convertible-note issuance should be present on EDGAR. The 7.00% coupon (vs the prior 0.25% coupon) is a meaningful cost-of-capital deterioration signal.

claims.claim_text: On November 6, 2025 Opendoor closed a Registered Direct Offering of 180,580,200 shares at $6.56 per share, concurrently repurchasing approximately $264 million principal of 2030 Notes for an aggregate repurchase price of approximately $1.2 billion (resulting in $933M recorded loss on debt extinguishment).
claims.source_quote: In November 2025, the Company entered into share purchase agreements with a limited number of purchasers ... providing for the issuance and sale by the Company of an aggregate of 180,580,200 shares of the common stock at a price of $6.56 per share (the Registered Direct Offering). Concurrent with the Registered Direct Offering, the Company entered into separate, privately negotiated transactions with the Purchasers, pursuant to which the Company agreed to repurchase an aggregate of approximately $264 million principal amount of the 2030 Notes for an aggregate repurchase price of approximately $1.2 billion ... recorded $933 million of loss on debt extinguishment
claims.subject: Opendoor Technologies Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: A November 2025 8-K and 424B5 prospectus should be retrievable. Magnitude of loss on extinguishment relative to net loss is the discriminator; structural distress signal.

proposed_connector.name: pacer.query_case_docket
proposed_connector.description: Federal court PACER docket retrieval for case-status and final-judgment verification on named civil cases.
proposed_connector.endpoint: https://pcl.uscourts.gov/pcl/index.jsf (PACER Case Locator) and per-court CM/ECF (e.g. https://ecf.azd.uscourts.gov)
proposed_connector.sample_invocation: PACER Case Locator search court=azd, case_no=2:22-CV-01717-MTL -> CM/ECF docket pull -> filter for 'Final Judgment' entry; alternatively use CourtListener RECAP archive (https://www.courtlistener.com/api/rest/v3/dockets/?docket_number=2:22-cv-01717) as a free mirror.
proposed_connector.rationale: Securities-class-action final disposition is an authoritative status only court dockets adjudicate; SEC filings are issuer-prepared and therefore self-referential. CourtListener / RECAP provides a free public mirror sufficient for binary final-judgment confirmation.
proposed_connector.estimated_cost: $0.10/page on PACER; free via CourtListener RECAP
proposed_connector.completeness: All federal district / appellate court cases; bankruptcy and state cases excluded

claims.extraction_notes: EDGAR fulltext could find references but not adjudicate the docket entry; PACER/CourtListener is the authoritative registry.

claims.source_quote: We operate our mortgage business through our wholly-owned mortgage subsidiary. To grow our mortgage business, we expect that such entity will depend, in part, on having access to sufficient capital. ... we expect that substantially all mortgage loans we originate will be sold into the secondary market.
claims.subject: Opendoor mortgage subsidiary

proposed_connector.name: nmls.query_consumer_access
proposed_connector.description: NMLS Consumer Access — Nationwide Multistate Licensing System public registry for state-licensed mortgage companies and individual MLOs.
proposed_connector.sample_invocation: GET https://www.nmlsconsumeraccess.org/Home.aspx/CompanySearch with name='Opendoor' -> parse company-detail page for state licenses and license-status fields
proposed_connector.rationale: State mortgage-origination licensing has no SEC analog; NMLS is the authoritative public registry for non-bank mortgage lender licensing status across all 50 states.
proposed_connector.completeness: All state-licensed non-bank mortgage companies and individual MLOs (NMLS-participating states, which is all 50)

claims.extraction_notes: Mortgage subsidiary name not stated explicitly in the slice; Phase 2 may need to search 'Opendoor Home Loans' / 'Opendoor Mortgage' in NMLS Consumer Access. Adjudication is existence + state coverage of active mortgage licenses.

claims.claim_text: Opendoor self-describes as 'the largest U.S. iBuyer' with over 294,000 homes bought and sold cumulatively since 2014, and sold over 11,700 homes generating $4.4 billion in revenue in 2025.
claims.source_quote: We are a leading e-commerce platform for residential real estate transactions and the largest U.S. iBuyer. ... Since launch, customers have demonstrated their desire for our digital, on-demand real estate solution with over 294,000 homes bought and sold by Opendoor across the United States. In 2025, we sold over 11,700 homes and generated $4.4 billion in revenue
claims.subject: Opendoor Technologies Inc.
claims.object_value: 294,000 cumulative homes; 11,700+ homes sold in 2025; $4.4B 2025 revenue
claims.extraction_notes: Relative-scale claim ('largest') adjudicated by counting comparable iBuyer disclosures from competitor 10-Ks (Offerpad Solutions CIK 0001825024). Pure unit counts without external registry — EDGAR FT cross-check is the best available substitute given there is no federal iBuyer registry.
